name: Piper PA-30/39 Twin Comanche
variants: PA-30B / PA-30C (turbo option, tip tanks, six-seat)
summary: Slim, economical four-to-six-seat retractable-gear twin built 1963–1972, the twin-engine sibling of the Comanche and a popular owner-flown light twin.

wings: Low, straight constant-chord wing with no taper
Later models often carry small tip tanks on the wingtips
engines: Two small Lycoming engines in slim, compact nacelles
fuselage: Slim, sleek cabin with a sloping nose and a flat-topped canopy line
tail: Strongly raked fin with a squared-off top

tellTales: Small, slim twin with a straight constant-chord wing
Strongly raked, square-topped fin with a low stabilator
Narrow sloping nose on a compact cabin

confusedWith.howToTell: The Apache has a blunter, rounder nose and a deeper, boxier cabin on a thick wing; the Twin Comanche is slimmer with a sloping nose.
The single-engine Comanche has one engine in the nose; the Twin Comanche has an engine on each wing.
The Travel Air has a tall, upright, squared-off fin and a tapered wing; the Twin Comanche has a raked fin and a straight wing with no taper.
